contract.interface:
Supplied rational J0,A,K,h and gamma satisfy 0<=J0<=(1-gamma)I, K>0, A in Q^{r x n},0<gamma<=1. For x in {-1,+1}^n, p(x) proportional exp[0.5 x^T J0 x+0.5(Ax)^T K(Ax)+h^T x]. Positive means PSD, not entrywise nonnegative; J0 need not have zero diagonal or obey a Dobrushin row-sum condition. The proposed randomized compiler outputs full-discrete TV-epsilon sampling and additive-epsilon log Z (relative partition accuracy), with preprocessing confidence 1-delta. Total rational input bits B include gamma. The recovered note's bound is [n^2{sqrt(n)+log(n/epsilon)}/epsilon]^{O(r)} poly(B,n,gamma^-1,epsilon^-1,log(1/delta)); the pasted report displays the looser n in place of sqrt(n). Polynomial-time scope requires fixed rank and inverse-polynomial residual gap. Rank reduction is charged rational linear algebra; tiny binary gamma is not free. No numerical spike/field norm or reciprocal Gaussian-cell mass appears in the claimed bound. Independent correctness and a certified full implementation are unestablished.

Classical Gaussian lifting uses ell(y)=h+A^T y and F(y,x)=exp[-0.5 y^T K^-1 y+0.5 x^T J0 x+ell(y)^T x], total mass C_K Z, C_K=(2pi)^(r/2)sqrt(det K). Hyperplanes divide each field in [-L,L] into bins of width Delta. On cell C, c_C clips to +/-L or rounds to a bin midpoint, b=n Delta/2, and D(y)=sum_i(|ell_i(y)|-L)_+=d_C^T y+e_C retains all excess energy. Q(y,x)=exp[-0.5 y^T K^-1 y+D(y)] exp[0.5 x^T J0 x+c_C^T x]. Let R=max_i sum_{j!=i}|J0ij| and rho=n exp[-2(L-R)]. Conditional wrong-sign bounds, without independence, give (1-rho)e^-b<=Z0(ell)/(e^D Z0(c_C))<=e^b. Exact ideal acceptance a=exp[(ell-c_C)^T x-D-b] obeys 0<=a<=1,Qa=e^-b F and conditional expected acceptance>=(1-rho)e^-2b.

The normalized spin envelope has TV(q_X,p)<=rho+2b and log-partition bias<=b-log(1-rho). Choose L=ceil R+ceil log2(8n/epsilon), Nbins=ceil(16nL/epsilon); b<=epsilon/16,rho<=epsilon/8. There are m=n(Nbins+1) hyperplanes, M<=sum_{j=0}^r binom(m,j) cells. Weights W_C=G_C Z0(c_C), G_C=integral_C exp[-0.5 y^T K^-1 y+d_C^T y+e_C]dy, form a finite mixture of bounded-field laws. A draw selects a cell and one base spin sample; no latent sample, rejection or metastable tunnelling remains at output time. The constant-grid ideal rejection primitive separately has acceptance>=3e^-1/4/4; it is not a fully implemented exact finite-bit sampler.

Gaussian masses are acquired, not free rare-event oracles. Rational constrained quadratic minimization finds y_*; subtracting its mode gives convex phi>=0. For V(t)=vol{y in C:phi(y)<=t}, V(t)<=t^r V(1) at t>=1, I>=e^-1 V(1), I=integral e^-t V(t)dt. A positive layer-cake sum with cutoff O(r^2+log(1/eta)) and mesh O(eta) reduces relative integration to charged convex-volume calls without cancellation or division by unknown event probability. Rational LP, slack bounds and quadratic gradients provide polynomial-bit inner/outer radius guarantees; classical rounding/grid algorithms are imported. Exact large rational prefactors and logarithmic weights avoid uncharged expanded digits. The base spectral gap >=gamma (continuous time) gives bounded-field heat-bath sampling, and n-stage bounded-variable annealing estimates Z0; its conservative arithmetic cost is O(n^5/[gamma eta^2] [n(L+1)+log(n/eta)] log(n/zeta)), plus bit overhead. J0=0 is a simpler product base.

Preprocessing charges arrangement O(mM) rational LP calls, M Gaussian integrals and base partitions, normalization, finite randomness and precision. Per-cell log error O(epsilon), not epsilon/M, controls mixture error; confidence costs log M. Memory is M poly(n,r,B,log epsilon^-1,log delta^-1) bits. Each draw pays categorical work, base sampling and n-spin output. The output partition representation is log Z or compact scientific notation. Approximate-model transfer requires a separately acquired uniform energy bound, e.g. n||J-Jhat||op/2+||h-hhat||1<=u. Exact factor acquisition/calibration and physical equilibration time are not supplied by the computational theorem.

Koehler-Lee-Risteski already supply full-TV/relative-partition low-rank algorithms using Gaussian lifting. Proposed improvement is over their displayed numerical-strength guarantee, not a lower bound on their algorithm or exhaustive priority clearance. Exchangeable magnetization aggregation may be preferable. Naive clipping fails; negative spikes have known rank-one hardness; diagonal shifts do not make high-rank sampling easy. m^{Theta(r)} is this representation's cost, not a universal lower bound. Gaussian-crossing N726/N730 are not premises or the same computational family. Source proof candidates, partial rank-one implementation and failed numerical attempts are preserved separately. General certified implementation, independent correctness, priority, practical advantage and technological readiness remain UNKNOWN.
